question: Unacceptable and unbelievable scenes were played out outside the court that was hearing the application by the elected Mayor of Himara, Fredi Beleri, for permission to take the oath of office as mayor and to be released from prison under restrictive conditions after eight months of unjust and contrived pre-trial detention.

On arrival at the court, Vangjel Dule, opposition MP and the only MP from the Greek national minority, found himself being targeted by a group of Albanian nationalists. He was subjected to unacceptable abuse and verbal attacks, and his physical integrity was put at serious risk, with the aim of undermining his support for the Mayor of Himara, Fredi Beleri.
In statements that he made, he charged the Albanian Government with being the moral instigator of the attack against him. In view of this: 1.
Is the Commission aware of the above facts?
What steps does it propose to take regarding the unacceptable attack on an elected Member of the Parliament of Albania, which is a country in the process of accession to the European Union?
answer: The Commission attaches great importance to the rule of law and fundamental rights. Through the enlargement process and the EU-Albania Stabilisation and Association Agreement (1), the Commission is closely following reforms on the rule of law, the strengthening and protection of the fundamental rights in Albania and provides policy recommendations in that regard.

As part of this continuous work, the Commission closely monitors and supports the consolidation of democracy, rule of law and fundamental rights in Albania as part of the European integration process of the country.

On the protection of national minorities, the Commission noted in its 2023 Report on Albani a (2) that the adoption of the remaining pieces of implementing legislation related to the 2017 framework law did not advance, notably the adoption implementing legislation on the rights of persons belonging to minorities pertaining to self-identification and the use of minority languages are pending.

The Commission also pointed to the need to strengthen the capacities of the State Committee on National Minorities. The Commission recalls that any attack or intimidation against elected officials has no place in democratic societies. The Commission does not comment on allegations regarding individual cases.

The Commission will continue to closely monitor and report on developments and progress in needed reforms in Albania in the context of its EU accession process, including on protection of fundamental rights.
